findings.summary: The truncated, unbalanced ADR-010 status cell in docs/decisions/00-index.md is now a complete, balanced, and accurate summary of the relation recorded in ADR-010.md.
findings.detail: The documentation review recorded the pre-fix cell as 'Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015: the SkiaSharp library' -- an unterminated parenthesis that reproduced only the first clause of ADR-010.md's Status block, and the only unbalanced row in the file. The new cell reads: 'Accepted (partially superseded by ADR-015: the decisions that the plugin package must carry the managed `SkiaSharp.dll` and native `libSkiaSharp.so` and must not load a system Skia library are superseded, while the SkiaSharp library choice, bundled font, PNG/color handling, host/source boundary, configuration, and testing strategy remain in force; the renderer-configuration clauses that keep geometry, placement, and scale code-owned are superseded by ADR-019 (v1.1))'. I verified this against ADR-010.md:3-9 clause by clause: the six in-force items (SkiaSharp library choice, bundled font, PNG/color handling, host/source boundary, configuration, testing strategy) all appear; the two superseded ADR-015 decisions appear; the ADR-019 renderer-configuration supersession appears. Nothing is dropped and nothing is invented, so it is neither an overclaim nor an underclaim of the recorded relation. I independently confirmed balance with `awk` paren counting over all index rows (lines 9-37): no unbalanced row remains (pre-fix only line 18 was flagged). The row count is 29, matching 29 ADR files, and check-docs' 'decisions index (29 ADRs)' section passes. The '(v1.1)' tag on ADR-019 matches the ADR-019 row's own 'Accepted (v1.1; ...)' and the ADR-009 row's usage; ADR-015 is left untagged, matching its own row. The pre-fix cell was not rewritten from a source outside the record, and docs/decisions/ADR-010.md itself is unedited, so the immutability rule for ADR text holds; the review's own instruction not to rewrite ADR decision text was respected. The 'consider adding a check-docs guard' clause of the finding was advisory and is recorded as informational below.

findings.summary: Neither closed finding is covered by an automated guard: check-docs validates only the decisions-index row count, and the data-model note prose has no guard, so the class of defect can recur undetected.
findings.detail: F-21.2-D1's fix text said to 'consider adding a check-docs guard that rejects an unbalanced parenthesis or an unterminated status cell in the decisions index so the class cannot recur' -- advisory ('consider'), and the worker explicitly did not add one and recorded the gap honestly in its test_sensitivity field. I confirmed the gap is real: scripts/check-docs.sh's decisions section compares only `adr_rows` to `adr_files`, and no check inspects cell balance or status-cell termination. The 12.1/Phase 4 note prose has no guard at all, so sensitivity can only be shown by inspection against the file's own convention. This is a pre-existing guardrail limitation, not a regression: the attempt-1 reviewer recorded the same gap, and the worker demonstrated sensitivity for the decisions index by seeding a row-count violation and observing check-docs exit 1. Neither finding's closure depends on a guard.
